zh.title: 華航A350為何不飛松山－羽田？跑道長度不是唯一問題　關鍵在翼展與停機位
zh.summary: 華航第三架前四川航空A350-900（B-18923）首航桃園－成田，引發航迷敲碗松山－羽田。民航局現行飛航指南顯示松山跑道長2,605公尺，停機位最大機型以A330-300、777-200等為主；A350-900翼展64.75公尺，超過既有大型機停機位列示機型。華航未公布未派A350飛松山的個別原因，地面設施適用性是重要考量。
body: 中華航空新加入的Airbus A350-900（B-18923）於10月22日以CI104班機首度載客，自臺灣桃園國際機場（TPE）飛往東京成田國際機場（NRT）。消息引起航迷討論，也有人好奇：同樣是飛東京，為何不安排這架新成員飛松山機場往返羽田？從民航局公布的機場資料觀察，決定廣體客機能否定期使用特定機場，除了航程與跑道長度，更涉及翼展、停機位、滑行路線及飛航性能等一整套條件。

民航局目前生效的《臺北飛航情報區飛航指南》（2026年10月1日版本）顯示，臺北松山機場（TSA）10／28跑道長2,605公尺、寬60公尺。其停機位資料將3、9號位的最大機型列為A330-300，4至7號位則列為波音777-200，並未列出A350-900。這些是公開的標準機坪配置資料，不能單憑此斷言A350在任何情況下都不得降落松山，但足以說明若要安排常態營運，必須先處理停機位及地面動線的適用性問題。
差距有多大？空中巴士官方公布A350-900翼展為64.75公尺，A330-300則為60.30公尺，兩者相差4.45公尺。即使同屬大型雙走道客機，新增的翼展仍可能影響翼尖與鄰近停機位、滑行道及其他設施的安全間隔。松山機場飛航指南也載明，部分滑行路徑僅供翼展36公尺以下的航機使用。因此，不能只看飛機能否在跑道上落地，還要確認落地後是否有合適的滑行及停靠安排。
另一方面，2,605公尺跑道並不等於所有A350都「絕對無法起降」。實際可用起降性能須依機型、起降重量、氣溫、風、跑道狀況、障礙物與特定程序計算，航空公司還須完成相關運作評估。松山機場位於市區，民航局亦將其列為受到地形及建築物障礙影響的特殊機場，航機必須符合離場爬升梯度等規定。現有公開資料不足以確認華航A350在何種載重及條件下可於松山安全起降，更不能將跑道長度當作唯一判斷標準。

至於羽田機場（HND）本身，A350並非陌生機型。日本航空現已安排A350-1000執飛羽田出發的國際航班，顯示問題不能簡化成「羽田不收A350」。華航既有松山－羽田定期航班，包括CI220及CI222，公開班表目前仍以A330-300執飛。從航機分配角度看，新加入的A350選擇先在既有桃園－成田航線投入服務，也符合以已具備相應設施的機場承接新機營運的邏輯；但這屬於依公開資料所做的分析，並非華航公布的B-18923調度決策理由。
因此，對於「怎麼不飛松山－羽田」，較精確的回答是：松山機場的機坪、翼展及地面運作條件，讓A350與現行A330營運存在明顯差別，不能因為兩條東京航線的飛行時間相近，就認為可以直接替換機型。截至10月22日，尚未查得華航針對B-18923首航為何未選松山－羽田所發布的正式說明，也沒有足夠證據宣布該機型在松山全面禁止起降。未來是否有特殊安排或規劃變更，仍須以航空公司與主管機關公布資訊為準。

en.title: Why Isn't China Airlines Flying Its New A350 on Songshan–Haneda? Wingspan and Parking Stands Matter
en.summary: China Airlines' ex-Sichuan A350 B-18923 made its first revenue flight from Taoyuan to Narita rather than Songshan to Haneda. Taiwan's current aeronautical information lists Songshan's large-aircraft stands for A330-300s or 777-200s, while the A350-900 has a 64.75-meter wingspan. China Airlines has not disclosed the specific reason for this aircraft's route assignment.
body: China Airlines' newly introduced Airbus A350-900 B-18923 entered passenger service on October 22 as CI104 from Taiwan Taoyuan (TPE) to Tokyo Narita (NRT). Aviation enthusiasts have asked why the aircraft was not assigned to the airline's Taipei Songshan (TSA)–Tokyo Haneda (HND) route. Airport compatibility involves far more than the distance between the cities or runway length: wingspan, aircraft stands, taxi routes and performance requirements all matter.

Taiwan's currently effective aeronautical information publication, dated October 1, 2026, lists Songshan's Runway 10/28 as 2,605 meters long and 60 meters wide. Aircraft stand data specify the A330-300 as the maximum type for stands 3 and 9 and the Boeing 777-200 for stands 4 through 7; the A350-900 is not listed. This does not by itself establish an absolute prohibition on A350 landings, but it raises a practical question about the aircraft's suitability for routine ground operations.

According to Airbus, the A350-900 has a wingspan of 64.75 meters, compared with 60.30 meters for the A330-300: a difference of 4.45 meters. Extra wingspan can affect wingtip clearance from nearby stands, taxiways and infrastructure. Songshan's published operating information also limits certain taxilanes to aircraft with wingspans below 36 meters. Landing on the runway and safely taxiing to an approved stand are separate considerations.

A 2,605-meter runway alone does not prove that every A350 operation would be impossible. Performance depends on aircraft mass, temperature, wind, runway conditions, obstacles and relevant procedures. Songshan is designated a special airport due to terrain and building obstructions, with mandatory departure climb gradients. The public information reviewed here does not establish exactly which A350 loading conditions, if any, could support a specific Songshan operation.

Tokyo Haneda itself regularly accommodates A350 aircraft: Japan Airlines operates A350-1000 international flights from Haneda. Meanwhile, published schedules for China Airlines' Songshan–Haneda services CI220 and CI222 identify A330-300 aircraft. Assigning the newly received A350 to an established Taoyuan–Narita operation is consistent with existing infrastructure and fleet deployment patterns, although China Airlines has not identified these factors as its specific reason for B-18923's first flight assignment.

The most evidence-based answer is that Songshan's stand configurations and ground operating environment differ materially from those at Taoyuan, making substitution of an A350 for an A330 less straightforward than it may appear. As of October 22, no official China Airlines explanation for the specific B-18923 routing decision has been identified, nor is there a sound basis to claim that all A350 landings at Songshan are categorically prohibited.
